fi-amphiprion-ocellaris.title: Ocellaris Clownfish (all designer morphs)
fi-amphiprion-ocellaris.summary: The classic 'Nemo' clownfish. Hardy, captive-bred and reef-safe. Every designer morph has the same care.
rows: About 4 in (11 cm max). Sold at about 1.25–1.5 in
15 gal or larger for one fish or a pair
Peaceful to semi-aggressive. Don't mix with other clownfish species
Keep one or a bonded pair. The larger fish becomes the female
Yes. Without an anemone it may host in a coral, which can irritate that coral
Frozen mysis or other marine frozen foods plus pellets, including some algae-based food. Feed 1–3 small meals a day
Indo-West Pacific reefs. These are captive-bred
notes: An anemone is optional. Bubble tip anemones are the usual host if you want one, but research their needs first.
Long-finned morphs do best in low to moderate flow.

fi-pseudochromis-aldabraensis.title: Arabian Neon Dottyback (tank raised)
fi-pseudochromis-aldabraensis.summary: A captive-bred dottyback (Arabian or Neon Dottyback).
rows: About 3 in; wild record 10 cm (3.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep singly unless the tank is very large
Carnivore. Meaty carnivore foods; once a day in a reef
Indian Ocean: Aldabra, Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. This SKU is tank raised

fi-amphiprion-clarkii.title: Clark's Clownfish (tank raised)
fi-amphiprion-clarkii.summary: A sturdy clownfish. This SKU is a captive-bred dark ('black') form.
rows: About 6 in; wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Keep one or a pair; semi-aggressive toward other clownfish
Omnivore. Mysis, brine shrimp and other meaty foods plus herbivore preparations
Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf to Western Australia, throughout the Indo-Australian Archipelago and in the western Pacific at the islands of Melanesia and Micronesia. This SKU is tank raised

fi-pseudochromis-fridmani.title: Orchid Dottyback (tank raised)
fi-pseudochromis-fridmani.summary: A vivid purple dottyback, captive-bred. Wild fish live in colonies near ledges and pick plankton.
rows: About 3 in; wild record 6.3 cm (2.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Western Indian Ocean: known only from the Red Sea. This SKU is tank raised
notes: Wants many hiding places; swims more openly once settled.

fi-elacatinus-figaro.title: Yellowline Goby (tank raised)
fi-elacatinus-figaro.summary: A tiny cleaner goby with gold lines, from Brazil. Wild export has stopped, so captive-bred fish are the supply.
rows: wild record 3.4 cm (1.3 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Carnivore. Small meaty foods; may clean other fish
Southwest Atlantic: Brazil. This SKU is tank raised

fi-amphiprion-percula.title: Percula Clownfish (Picasso, tank raised)
fi-amphiprion-percula.summary: The true percula clownfish. This SKU is a tank-raised designer (Picasso) form. Hardy and reef safe.
rows: About 3 in; wild record 11 cm (4.3 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep one or a pair; the larger fish is the female
Omnivore. Meaty foods plus herbivore preparations
Western Pacific: Queensland and Melanesia including northern Great Barrier Reef, northern New Guinea, New Britain, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu. This SKU is tank raised

fi-amphiprion-frenatus.title: Tomato Clownfish (tank raised)
rows: About 5 in; wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep one or a pair; the female is the larger fish
Omnivore. Meaty foods plus herbivore preparations
Western Pacific: Gulf of Thailand to southwestern Palau, north to southern Japan, south to Java, Indonesia. This SKU is tank raised
notes: May use a coral as a host if there is no anemone.

fi-elacatinus-oceanops.title: Neon Goby
fi-elacatinus-oceanops.summary: A tiny cleaner goby from Florida, the Gulf and the western Caribbean, dark blue with an electric-blue stripe. It cleans parasites off other fish and pairs readily.
rows: About 2 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 5 cm (2 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: frozen brine shrimp, mysis shrimp, chopped shrimp, clam, scallop, krill, marine fish flesh, marine flake or pellet
Western Central Atlantic: southern Florida to Texas (USA) southward to Belize. This SKU is tank raised
notes: Territorial with its own kind unless a bonded pair; mated pairs often spawn in aquariums.
Most larger fish leave a cleaner alone, but avoid predators big enough to eat it.

fi-elacatinus-puncticulatus.title: Red Head Goby
fi-elacatinus-puncticulatus.summary: A small cleaner goby from the eastern Pacific (Gulf of California to Ecuador) with a red-orange head. Peaceful and easy, and the TRG SKU is tank raised.
rows: About 2 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 5 cm (2 in) TL (FishBase)
Eastern Central Pacific: Gulf of California to Ecuador. This SKU is tank raised

fi-elacatinus-evelynae.title: Sharknose Goby (Tank Raised)
fi-elacatinus-evelynae.summary: A tiny Caribbean cleaner goby with a yellow stripe on the head that turns neon blue along the body. In the wild it runs cleaning stations, picking parasites off larger fish. This one is tank raised.
rows: About 1.5 in (ORA adult size); wild record 4 cm (1.6 in) TL (FishBase)
Takes a wide range of frozen and dry foods; wild fish eat parasites and dead skin picked off other fish, plus zooplankton
Western Atlantic: Bahamas and the Lesser Antilles to the northern coast of South America. This SKU is tank raised
notes: A good choice for peaceful reef tanks.
